subdomains.title: Cybersecurity Roles and Responsibilities
subdomains.objective: To ensure that roles and responsibilities are defined for all parties participating in implementing the cloud cybersecurity controls, including the roles and responsibilities of the head of the CSP and CST or his/her delegate, referred to in these controls as “Authorizing Official”.

controls.desc: In addition to the ECC control 1-4-1, the Authorizing Official shall also identify, document and approve:
Cybersecurity roles and RACI assignment for all stakeholders of the cloud services, including the Authorizing Official’s roles and responsibilities.
controls.evidence: • Cloud Cybersecurity Roles and Responsibilities and RACI matrix defined, approved, and documented within the related Service Level Agreements (SLAs) between CSP and CST.

subdomains.title: Cybersecurity Risk Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure managing cybersecurity risks in a methodological approach in order to protect the CSP’s and CST’s information and technology assets as per organizational policies and procedures, and related laws and regulations.

controls.desc: The cybersecurity risk management methodology mentioned in ECC Subdomain 1-5 shall also include for the CST, as a minimum:
Defining acceptable risk levels for the cloud services.
controls.evidence: • Catalogue of cloud services with assigned acceptable risk level.

controls.desc: Considering data and information classification accredited by the CST in the cybersecurity risk management methodology.
controls.evidence: • Cybersecurity Risk Management Methodology with a unique approach to data classes.

controls.desc: Developing a cybersecurity risk register for cloud services, and monitoring it periodically according to the risks.
controls.evidence:
• Cybersecurity Cloud Services Risk Register.
• Cybersecurity Cloud Services Risk Register review plan.

subdomains.title: Compliance with Cybersecurity Standards, Laws and Regulations
subdomains.objective: To ensure that the CSPs’ and CSTs’ cybersecurity program is in compliance with related laws and regulations.

controls.desc: In addition to ECC control 1-7-1, the CST legislative and regulatory compliance shall include, as a minimum, the following requirement:
Continuous or real-time compliance monitoring of the CSP with relevant cybersecurity legislation and contractual clauses.
controls.evidence:
• CSP compliance reports verified periodically.
• Reports or evidence demonstrating the monitoring of compliance within contracts.

subdomains.title: Cybersecurity in Human Resources
subdomains.objective: To ensure that cybersecurity risks and requirements related to personnel (employees and contractors) are managed efficiently prior to employment, during employment, and after termination/separation as per organizational policies and procedures, and related laws and regulations.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 1-9-3, the following requirement shall be covered prior to the professional relationship of staff with the CST, as a minimum:
Screening or vetting candidates for personnel positions with access to sensitive Cloud Service functions (Key Management, Service Administration, and Access Control).
controls.evidence:
• Catalogue of privileged user roles, including Key Management, Service Administration, and Access Control.
• Screening/Vetting process defined for candidates who use these user roles.

subdomains.title: Asset Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure that the CSP and CST have an accurate and detailed inventory of information and technology assets in order to support the organization’s cybersecurity and operational requirements and maintain the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and technology assets.

controls.desc: In addition to the controls in ECC control 2-1, the CST shall cover the following additional control for asset management, as a minimum:
Inventory of all cloud services and information and technology assets related to the cloud services.
controls.evidence: • Inventory of cloud services and related data and assets.

subdomains.title: Identity and Access Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure secure and restricted logical access to information and technology assets in order to prevent unauthorized access and allow only authorized access for users that is necessary to accomplish assigned tasks.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-2-3, the CST shall cover the following additional subcontrols for identity and access management requirements, as a minimum:
Identity and access management for all cloud credentials throughout their full lifecycle.
controls.evidence: • Cloud Identity Lifecycle process defined.

controls.desc: Confidentiality of cloud user identification, cloud credentials, and cloud access-rights information, including the requirement for users to keep them private (for employees, third parties, and CST personnel).
controls.evidence: • Login screens available only through encrypted channels, such as TLS.

controls.desc: Secure session management, including session authenticity, session lockout, and session timeout termination.
controls.evidence: • Session management system configured with session lockouts and session timeouts.

controls.desc: Multi-factor authentication for privileged cloud users.
controls.evidence:
• Multi-factor authentication policy assigned to privileged users or groups of users.
• List of privileged cloud users.

controls.desc: Formal process to detect and prevent unauthorized access to cloud services, such as a threshold for unsuccessful login attempts.
controls.evidence: • Impossible-travel scenarios detected and prevented.

subdomains.title: Information System and Information Processing Facilities Protection
subdomains.objective: To ensure the protection of information systems and information processing facilities, including workstations and infrastructures, against cyber risks.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-3-3, the CST shall cover the following additional subcontrol for information-system and processing-facilities protection, as a minimum:

Verifying that the CSP isolates the community cloud services provided to CSTs (government organizations and CNI organizations) from any other cloud computing provided to organizations outside the scope of work.
controls.evidence: • CSP community-cloud isolation verified through agreed means between the CST and CSP.

subdomains.title: Networks Security Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure the protection of the CSP’s and CST’s networks from cyber risks.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-5-3, the CST shall cover the following additional subcontrol for network security management, as a minimum:
Protecting the connection channel with the CSP.
controls.evidence:
• Disaster Recovery Plan for CST-to-CSP connections.
• Network diagram illustrating the implementation of cybersecurity practices to protect network communication between the CST and CSP.

subdomains.title: Mobile Devices Security
subdomains.objective: To ensure the protection of mobile devices, including laptops, smartphones, and tablets, from cyber risks and ensure secure handling of the CSP’s and CST’s information, including sensitive information, while utilizing mobile devices.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-6-3, the CST shall cover the following additional subcontrol for mobile-device security, as a minimum:
Data sanitization and secure disposal for end-user devices with access to cloud services.
controls.evidence: • Approved and implemented data-sanitization and device-disposal tools and methods.

subdomains.title: Data and Information Protection
subdomains.objective: To ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the CSP’s and CST’s data and information as per organizational policies and procedures, and related laws and regulations.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-7-3, the CST shall cover the following additional subcontrols for protecting CST data and information in cloud computing, as a minimum:
Exit Strategy to ensure means for secure disposal of data upon termination or expiry of the contract with the CSP.
controls.evidence:
• Cloud Exit Strategy documented.
• Evidence confirming the existence of a service provided by the CSP that allows the CST to securely dispose of data or, at a minimum, a contractual clause granting the CST the ability to dispose of the data.

controls.desc: Using secure means to export and transfer data and virtual infrastructure.
controls.evidence: • Defined requirements and applied security measures relevant to the export and transfer of data and virtual infrastructure.

subdomains.title: Cryptography
subdomains.objective: To ensure the proper and efficient use of cryptography to protect information assets as per policies, procedures, and related laws and regulations.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-8-3, the CST shall cover the following additional subcontrols for cryptography, as a minimum:
Technical mechanisms and cryptographic primitives for strong encryption, in accordance with the advanced level in the National Cryptographic Standards (NCS-1:2020).
controls.evidence: • Cryptographic standard document.

controls.desc: Encryption of data and information transferred to or transferred out of the cloud according to relevant legal and regulatory requirements.
controls.evidence: • Hybrid cloud connectivity encryption.

subdomains.title: Vulnerability Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure timely detection and effective remediation of technical vulnerabilities to prevent or minimize the probability of exploiting these vulnerabilities to launch cyberattacks against the CSP and CST.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-10-3, the CST shall cover the following additional subcontrols for vulnerability management, as a minimum:
Assessing and remediating vulnerabilities in cloud services at least once every three months.
controls.evidence:
• Document outlining the establishment and assurance of the implementation of a Vulnerability Management Policy encompassing cloud computing.
• Report assessing and addressing vulnerabilities related to cloud services at least once every three months.

controls.desc: Management safeguards for vulnerabilities notified by the CSP.
controls.evidence:
• Document outlining the establishment and assurance of the implementation of a Vulnerability Management Policy encompassing cloud computing.
• Report on managing vulnerabilities notified to the CST by the CSP, including the remediation process.

subdomains.title: Cybersecurity Event Logs and Monitoring Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure timely collection, analysis, and monitoring of cybersecurity event logs for the proactive detection and effective management of cyberattacks to prevent or minimize the impact on the CSP’s and CST’s business.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-12-3, the CST shall cover the following additional subcontrols for cybersecurity event logs and monitoring management, as a minimum:
Activating and collecting login event logs and cybersecurity event logs on assets related to cloud services.
controls.evidence: • Cloud Services cybersecurity event log.

controls.desc: Monitoring shall include all activated cybersecurity logs on the CST’s cloud services.
controls.evidence: • Cybersecurity event logs monitored.

subdomains.title: Key Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure secure management of the CSP’s and CST’s cryptographic keys to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and technical assets.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for key management within the CST shall be identified, documented, and approved.
controls.evidence:
• Key Management cybersecurity requirements documented and formally approved.
• Results of the periodic review.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for key management within the CST shall be applied.
controls.evidence:
• Cybersecurity requirements for Encryption Key Management documented and formally approved.
• Document outlining procedures for reporting standard violations.

controls.desc: In addition to ECC subcontrol 2-8-3-2, cybersecurity requirements for key management within the CST shall cover, at a minimum, the following:
Ensure well-defined ownership for cryptographic keys.
controls.evidence:
• Identified cryptographic keys and owners.
• Results of the periodic review.

controls.desc: A secure data-retrieval mechanism in case a cryptographic encryption key is lost, such as backup of keys and enforcement of trusted key storage strictly external to the cloud.
controls.evidence: • Cryptographic key-retrieval plan.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for key management within the CST shall be applied and reviewed periodically.
controls.evidence: • Cybersecurity requirements for Key Management reviewed regularly.

subdomains.title: Cybersecurity Resilience Aspects of Business Continuity Management (BCM)
subdomains.objective: To ensure the inclusion of cybersecurity resiliency requirements within the CSP’s and CST’s business continuity management and to remediate and minimize impacts on systems, information processing facilities, and critical e-services from disasters caused by cybersecurity incidents.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 3-1-3, the CST shall cover the following additional subcontrol for cybersecurity resilience aspects of business continuity management, as a minimum:
Developing and implementing disaster recovery and business continuity procedures related to cloud computing in a secure manner.
controls.evidence:
• Disaster Recovery Procedure/Plan for cloud computing.
• Business Continuity Procedure/Plan for cloud computing.
